title: Styling, Images & SEO
description: Polish the UI with Tailwind, add responsive images with next/image, and implement full metadata for every page.

slides.title: Tailwind: From Scratch to Styled 🎨
slides.content:
# Utility Classes Everywhere

Since we used `--tailwind` during creation, Tailwind is already set up.

We'll add:

* A responsive navbar with mobile menu.
* Card layout for post list.
* Prose typography for post content.
* A dark mode toggle (optional).

Tailwind's utility classes make it easy to build a cohesive design without leaving JSX.

slides.title: Navbar Component (components/Navbar.js)
Optimised Images with next/image 🖼️
slides.content:
# Adding Hero Images to Posts

If a post has a cover image, we can use the `Image` component:

```jsx
import Image from 'next/image';

<Image src={post.image} alt={post.title} width={800} height={400} priority />
```

* `priority` loads it eagerly (above the fold).
* Automatic WebP conversion.
* Lazy loading for off‑screen images.

Don't forget to add the domain to `next.config.js` if the image comes from an external source.

slides.title: Image Domain Config (next.config.js)
slides.content: Allow images from a CDN or external source.

quizData.question: What does the `priority` prop on `next/image` do?

options.text: Preloads the image, disables lazy loading, and marks it as high priority for LCP
Downloads the image before the page loads

quizData.explanation: `priority` is used for the largest contentful paint image to ensure it loads quickly and avoids layout shift.

slides.title: SEO with Metadata API 🔍
Root Layout Metadata (app/layout.js)
slides.content: Set a default title template for all pages.

quizData.question: If a child page sets `title: 'About'`, what will the final `<title>` tag be using the template above?
quizData.explanation: The `template` replaces `%s` with the child's title. So `About | MyBlog` is produced.

slides.title: Progressive Enhancement ✨
slides.content: Even with Tailwind and JavaScript, the core content is pre‑rendered. Search engines and users without JS still see all text. The styling is just the cherry on top.
